content.intended_use: Control the bias and gradient Lipschitz constant of the regularized max term.

map: Compactness and strong convex regularization give existence and uniqueness of the maximizer.
The source identifies the gradient as A*u(x), then writes first-order optimality inequalities after assuming differentiability of phi_hat and d2 for notation.
Apply (1.2) and the dual norm inequality to obtain the gradient Lipschitz constant.
proofs.omitted_details: The source's phrase 'without loss of generality' for differentiability is not expanded there. The separate local proof below avoids that assumption.

proofs.full_local_argument: Put alpha=mu sigma2>0 and H_x(u)=phi_hat(u)+mu d2(u)-<Ax,u>2. Compactness and continuity give a minimizer. H_x is alpha-strongly convex, hence its minimizer u_x is unique: distinct minimizers would have a midpoint with smaller value. For v∈Q2 and 0<t<1, minimality and strong convexity yield H_x(u_x)≤H_x((1-t)u_x+tv)≤(1-t)H_x(u_x)+tH_x(v)-(alpha/2)t(1-t)||v-u_x||2². Divide by t and let t decrease to zero to obtain H_x(v)-H_x(u_x)≥(alpha/2)||v-u_x||2². Apply this with v=u_y and the analogous inequality for H_y with v=u_x. Adding cancels phi_hat and d2 and gives alpha||u_x-u_y||2²≤<A(x-y),u_x-u_y>2≤a||x-y||1||u_x-u_y||2. If the optimizer difference is zero its bound is immediate; otherwise divide to obtain ||u_x-u_y||2≤(a/alpha)||x-y||1. Each objective inside the maximum defining f_mu is affine in x, so f_mu is convex; compactness also makes its value finite. At x and x+h, evaluating each maximum at the other's optimizer gives <Ah,u_x>2≤f_mu(x+h)-f_mu(x)≤<Ah,u_{x+h}>2. Consequently 0≤f_mu(x+h)-f_mu(x)-<A*u_x,h>1≤a||h||1||u_{x+h}-u_x||2≤(a²/alpha)||h||1². This proves Frechet differentiability with gradient A*u_x. The operator norm bound gives ||A*(u_x-u_y)||1*≤a||u_x-u_y||2≤(a²/alpha)||x-y||1, proving continuous differentiability and the claimed Lipschitz bound, also when a=0. Finally normalization and compactness give 0≤d2(u)≤D2 for all u∈Q2. Therefore for each u, <Ax,u>2-phi_hat(u)-mu d2(u)≤<Ax,u>2-phi_hat(u)≤<Ax,u>2-phi_hat(u)-mu d2(u)+mu D2. Taking maxima proves both bias inequalities. All conclusions follow without differentiability of phi_hat or d2.

assumptions: Q2 is nonempty, closed, bounded and convex in E2.
d2:Q2→R is continuous and sigma2-strongly convex relative to ||.||2: for u,v∈Q2 and t∈[0,1], d2((1-t)u+tv)≤(1-t)d2(u)+td2(v)-(sigma2/2)t(1-t)||u-v||2².
mu>0. Neither phi_hat nor d2 is assumed differentiable.
statement.conclusion: f_mu is finite, convex and continuously differentiable on all E1, with ∇f_mu(x)=A*u_mu(x). For all x,y∈E1, ||∇f_mu(x)-∇f_mu(y)||1*≤[a²/(mu sigma2)]||x-y||1. For every x∈E1, f_mu(x)≤f0(x)≤f_mu(x)+mu D2. This concerns the max term only; an additional f_hat in (2.2) requires its own regularity analysis.
statement.objects_and_definitions: E1,E2 are finite-dimensional real normed spaces with norms ||.||1,||.||2 and corresponding dual norms. A:E1→E2* is linear and <Ax,u>2=<A*u,x>1. Set a=||A||1,2=max_{||x||1=||u||2=1}<Ax,u>2. Define f0(x)=max_{u∈Q2}(<Ax,u>2-phi_hat(u)), f_mu(x)=max_{u∈Q2}(<Ax,u>2-phi_hat(u)-mu d2(u)), u_mu(x)=argmax of the latter, u0=argmin_Q2 d2 and D2=max_Q2 d2.
statement.parameter_domains: Arbitrary finite-dimensional real normed spaces; sigma2,mu∈(0,∞), A any linear map of the specified type, D2 finite and nonnegative. No positive lower bound on ||A|| or D2 is imposed.
statement.quantifiers_and_randomness: For every fixed choice of the stated data and every mu>0, the conclusions hold deterministically for all x,y∈E1. The maximizer u_mu(x) is unique for each x.

summary: Theorem 1 and (2.7): compact dual-domain strong convex regularization gives a convex C1 approximation with gradient Lipschitz bound ||A||1,2²/(mu sigma2) and uniform bias at most mu D2.
title: Gradient and uniform approximation of explicit max smoothing
use_when: Verify smoothness and bias for an explicitly represented max function; this is not an unrestricted Oracle Complexity bound.
